Subject: Private deployment micro-patch cadence and rollback runway (review)

Team —

Drafting a compact proposal for how we run micro-patches across Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). Goal: reduce blast radius and unit cost while keeping a fast rollback path for customers on pinned versions. Key points in the attached runbook:

- Version pinning model: allow customers to pin to a semver minor (e.g. 1.4.x) and we only move them within that minor unless they opt into a major.
- Micro-patch cadence: weekly canary for 1 controlled region, bi-weekly for remaining fleet.
- Maintenance window: propose 2-hour windows (customer-preferred) with a 45-minute canary + 75-minute ramp; customers can opt for zero-downtime rolling if they have multi-az.
- Rollback runway: automatic revert snapshot + KV cache invalidation within 15 minutes of failover decision; manual rollback path documented for on-prem where snapshot restore takes longer.
- Network isolation: pre-flight cordon, flow verify, and ingress ACL check before any change. See attached diagram.

Please review the runbook (private-micropatch-runbook-v1.2.pdf), the network diagram, and the canary checklist. Call out any blocking items (KMS rotation, customer cert expiry, or cross-account routing) and priority customers who need shorter windows.

TL;DR: seeking sign-off on the cadence and explicit rollback SLAs to include in customer comms.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: private-micropatch-runbook-v1.2.pdf (pdf), network-isolation-diagram-v3.png (png), canary-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Mar 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment micro-patch cadence and rollback runway (review)

Rohan —

Thanks for the tidy draft. A few operational notes from infra: 

- Network drain order: for multi-tenant VPCs we should drain non-production nodes first (staging -> canary -> prod), but for on-prem single-tenant hosts we should schedule maintenance during their low-IO windows; I'll add a per-customer drain-order appendix.
- KMS/Key rotation: if a customer rotates keys within the 48h prior to a patch we need to hold; add a gating check in the preflight script.
- Health-check thresholds: canary should use both readiness + perf baseline (p50/p95); if p95 degrades >25% within 30m, abort and start automated revert.

Inline comment: "15 minutes to rollback snapshot" is optimistic for some on-prem customers — we should categorize rollback types (fast revert, staged revert, manual restore) and add expected RTO per type.

I'll attach a short snippet to the runbook with network drain order and a gating checklist.

-karthik

Adding some customer ops context — especially for ACME Health (they prefer single 3-hour windows, Tues nights, and require a pre-approved rollback test plan).

- ACME constraint: their internal change board wants a 48-hour notice and a test run in a staging mirror. They also require evidence of network ACLs and PKI cert expiry checks.
- Suggest we include a "hold" state in the runbook where the change is staged but not executed until ACME verifies the staging snapshot (this reduces surprise restores).
- I've updated the canary-checklist.xlsx with the ACME-specific gating rows and the test-case IDs used by their team (see attached).

If we're going external with a maintenance proposal, I recommend a one-page customer matrix with the options: 2-hour fast window (default), 3-hour customer-preferred window (opt-in), or staged hold (requires mirror validation).

-Monica

Hi ACME team —

Forwarding our internal strawman for micro-patch cadence and rollback runway for Private deployments. TL;DR: we propose a staged canary followed by a fleet ramp, with an explicit fast-rollback path we can initiate automatically and a staged manual restore as fallback.

Proposed window for your environment: Tue 2025-03-25 02:00-05:00 PT (3-hour customer-preferred slot). We will run a staging rehearsal on Tue 2025-03-24 23:00-00:30 PT (this is a dry-run against your mirror).

Please confirm the window and the staging rehearsal. Note the preflight items below — we will not run if any are unmet: 
- Cert expiry within 7 days or KMS rotation within 48h.
- No outstanding cross-AZ routing clarifications.
- Signed runbook acceptance (we can capture via DocuSign).

Attachments: private-micropatch-runbook-v1.2.pdf, canary-checklist.xlsx, network-isolation-diagram-v3.png

Best,
Rohan

Rohan,

Thanks for the summary. Tue 2025-03-25 02:00-05:00 PT works for us for the main window, and the staging rehearsal time is fine. Two quick clarifications: 

1) Rollback SLA: what do you mean by "automated revert snapshot + KV cache invalidation within 15 minutes" for our on-prem nodes? Our restore runs from local SAN snapshots and typical RTO is ~45-60m.
2) Verification: please confirm the exact success criteria for canary (we need p50/p95 + error-rate < 0.5% over 30m).

If we can get the explicit confirmation on RTO expectations and the canary acceptance thresholds we will sign the runbook.

Regards,

Thanks — good questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- RTO/rollback: agree that 15m is optimistic for ACME on-prem; updated plan: for SAN-backed hosts we treat rollback as "fast-revert" (target 45m) with a separate manual restore path at 3h. I updated the runbook with categorized RTOs (fast: <=45m, staged: 45m-3h, manual: >3h).
- Canary acceptance: we'll use the metric gate you requested: p50/p95 within 15% of baseline and error-rate <0.5% over a 30m steady-state window. If any gate fails we abort and run automated revert and a post-mortem.

Next actions:
- I will create INF-6221 (Jira) and attach the signed runbook when we get DocuSign confirmation.
- Monica to coordinate the staging mirror rehearsal with ACME and confirm test-case IDs.
- Karthik to add the drain-order appendix and run the preflight key checks.

If everyone is aligned I will route the DocuSign with the updated RTO table and the customer matrix.

Thanks,
Rohan
